To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ground state neutron single-particle strength of the neutron-rich 46 Ar isotope is reduced by only 30% from that of the proton-rich 34 Ar isotope, and that the neutron single-particle strengths of the 1d(3/2), 2s(1/2) and 1d(5/2) orbitals in 46 Ar are all reduced by a similar amount.
the spectroscopic factor of a nucleus is not strongly dependent on neutron-proton asymmetries in light Ar isotopes.
spectroscopic factors for the ground state of 34Ar are similar to the values for 46Ar and are consistent with results obtained from systematic studies of (p, d), (p, t) and (p, p′) reactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the neutron-rich isotopes 46Ar and 34Ar.
the development of a new method for the measurement of neutron spectroscopic factors using transfer reactions.
the development of a new method of neutron spectroscopy using transfer reactions and its application to the study of the structure of exotic neutron-rich nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spectroscopic factors extracted from transfer reactions are consistent with those extracted from knockout reaction measurements.
the ground-state spectroscopic factors for the 34Ar(p, d)33Ar and 46Ar(p, d45Ar transfer reactions are consistent with the values expected from shell model calculations.
the neutron-proton symmetry energy does not have a strong effect on the spectroscopic factors of the valence neutron in the Ar isotopes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spectroscopic factors of the ground states in the 30Ar-34Ar isotopes are not significantly reduced from the values expected for a pure single-particle state.
the spectroscopic factor for the ground state of 46Ar is 0.65 ± 0.10, while the spectroscopic factor in 34Ar is 0 = 0.65 +0.10 -0.15.
the neutron-proton correlations do not depend strongly upon the asymmetry in the region of 32Ar-48Ar.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spectroscopic factors can be used as a tool to probe the structure of exotic nuclei.
the neutron-proton symmetry energy is not a major factor in determining spectroscopic factors in the Ar isotopes.
transfer reaction measurements are a useful tool for studying the structure of exotic nuclei and can be used in conjunction with knockout measurements for more complete understanding of structure.
